text:
emma: Quick kickoff — want to spin up a small 'benchmark lab' to lock the latency vs cost narrative for launch. Goal: three tight charts, 2 headline claim variants, and routing rules for inbound leads. Thoughts?
shane: love it. can we shard by workload type (short chat / long-context agent / embedding search)? keeps claims grounded. :100: 
maya: yes. suggest we also include a small sample calc for token cost at 1M qps-month equivalent so sales can quote quickly.
liam: agree on shards. For charts I'd do: 1) median + 95th latency vs per-1M-token cost, 2) throughput (RPS) vs $/hour for dedicated pools, 3) slice comparison (short vs long) showing batch/cache delta.
emma: perfect. can someone draft the chart specs and sample copy? i can take the webinar hook and inbound routing.
shane: grabbing chart specs now. minimal labels so creative can reuse.
shane: Chart A spec (latency vs cost):
```
x: median latency (ms)
y: $ per 1M tokens generated
points: model variants (rtd, quantized, cached)
annotation: p95 p99 callouts, note "cache active" vs "cold"
```
maya: Chart B spec (throughput economics):
```
x: throughput (RPS)
y: $/hour for a reserved pool (dedicated)
curves: autoscale vs fixed reserved
marker: SLA target line (100ms)
```
liam: Chart C (slice delta):
```
rows: short-chat, long-agent, embeddings-search
metric: tokens/req, median latency, unit $/req
bars: baseline vs with prefix cache vs with batching
```
emma: copy ideas (2 headline directions):
- Claim 1 (speed-first): "Ship fast experiences: median latency under 120ms while cutting inference costs by up to 3x vs naive serving."
- Claim 2 (economics-first): "Cut your inference spend without sacrificing responsiveness — predictable latency at lower unit cost."
shane: add a micro-example for the PR / social post: "Try our benchmark lab: short-chat demos at 100ms median, 2.4x cost savings w/ caching — see the sample calc."
maya: sample calc snippet for sales (one-liner): "1M tokens = 1M * $0.0004 = $400 (hosted); with caching & batching expected delta: -60% => $160."
liam: inbound routing rules (emma said she'd take, but tossing ideas):
- Demo request if team mentions "latency" or "p95" or asks "SLA" in sign-up form
- Enterprise lead if committed QPS > 2000 or wants private deploy
- Self-serve nurture for trial users showing <10k tokens/day but high tail latency alerts
- Route benchmark request to bench-bot automatically with attached sample charts
emma: my webinar hook draft: "Real production inference: How we balance p95 latency and unit economics — a lab-backed playbook." CTA: "Bring a sample prompt set; we'll slice it live."
shane: bench-bot can auto-generate the slice CSV if someone drops model + sample workload. wanna wire a demo before Wed?
bench-bot: auto-checklist: 1) upload sample prompts, 2) pick slices, 3) choose model variants, 4) run microbench (3 seeds), 5) output chart PNGs and CSV. use `/bench run` to start.
maya: timeline: mock charts by Tue EOD, copy + headline variants Wed morning, webinar outline Thu. Is that aggressive?
liam: doable if we keep the lab runs to small sample sets (<=5k tokens each). we can scale later for deeper appendix.
emma: ok nailed it. shane — you and liam pair on bench runs. maya on sample calc + sales one-pager. i'll draft webinar hook + landing copy. i'll drop the first drafts in this thread by Tue noon.
shane: on it. pairing in #eng-ml for tuning kernels if needed.
liam: linking a quick example command to run locally:
```bash
/bench run --model redwood-rtd-v1 --slices short,long,embed --tokens 5000 --seeds 3 --output /tmp/bench-output
```
maya: saved. also drafting two short email subject lines for inbound nurture: "See latency and cost in your workload" and "How fast can your app get? (bench results inside)"
emma: love those. closing loop: deliverables in thread: chart PNGs (A/B variants), sample calc, headline 2x variants, webinar outline, routing playbook bullets. keep messages short in deliverables doc so ops can clip for landing page copy.
shane: noted. will attach first PNGs once bench runs finish. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
bench-bot: run queued. ETA ~45m for first microbench.
liam: thanks team. see you in the thread with outputs. :rocket:
